objective: Bind the execution environment the provenance record claims into the release-eligibility verdict, so an edited, absent or incomplete environment claim cannot be promoted as evidence.
decision_supported: Is the environment field part of the eligibility contract, or a decorative label the validator may ignore?
acceptance: A provenance record whose environment differs from the one the run published is refused.
A record with the environment key absent is refused.
A record with a null environment is refused.
A record whose environment omits any field build_provenance always writes is refused.
A record with the environment build_provenance writes stays eligible.
Each refusal names a reason, not a bare false.
evidence: Before the change, three mutations all returned eligible: true with no reasons: environment replaced by {python: 9.9}, environment set to null, and the environment key deleted.
After the change those three are refused with REASON_ENVIRONMENT_INVALID or REASON_ENVIRONMENT_MISSING, and the untouched record stays eligible.
Deleting the new check makes six of the new cases fail; restoring it passes 27.
stop_conditions: A legitimate producer writes an environment without one of these fields; build_provenance always writes platform, python and machine, so that would be a producer bug to fix there.
risks_and_fallbacks: The check requires string values, so a producer that writes a non-string platform is refused rather than coerced; that is deliberate for an evidence claim.
The environment is judged for shape, not compared against this machine, because the verdict is about the record being self-consistent with what was published.
